description: A plotting area is **never negative and never NaN**, whatever arrived at it. Upstream's `layoutGroup` opens `width = Math.max(0, group.width || 0)` and `viewSizeLayout` repeats it, and the second one hands the result to `resizeView`, which writes it **back into the signal** — `view.signal(Width, width, Skip)` followed by `view.run('enter')`. So the rule is not merely that the layout uses zero: the `width` signal itself reads zero on the rerun, and everything downstream of it reads zero too. The two halves of `Math.max(0, group.width || 0)` are separate tests and this fixture carries one each. `width` resolves to **-120**, which the clamp takes; `height` resolves to **NaN** from `0 / 0`, which only the `|| 0` takes, because `Math.max(0, NaN)` is `NaN` and a size nothing can be laid out against would travel into every scale ranged on it. The observable is threefold. The band scale ranged on `"width"` and the linear scale ranged on `"height"` are both `[0, 0]`, so the rects have no width and sit on one line. The `half` and `tall` signals read the size *after* the write-back, which is why `half` is 0 rather than -60 and `tall` is 1 rather than NaN — a dependent signal is the only way to see that the write-back happened at all rather than the layout quietly using a different number. And the text mark prints both sizes, so a reading that clamps the layout and leaves the signal alone differs in the drawing rather than only in the geometry. A size declared as an ordinary negative property was already clamped; this is reachable only through a signal, which is how it went unnoticed.

text.signal: 'w ' + width + ' h ' + height + ' half ' + half + ' tall ' + tall
